questions.stem: What is a domain in Microsoft Fabric?

options.text: A capacity that only one department can use
A logical grouping of workspaces, usually by business area, used to organize and govern data
A network boundary that blocks traffic between workspaces
A type of lakehouse that holds master data

questions.explanation: Domains group workspaces by business area, such as Sales or Finance, so data can be organized and governed the way the business is, in the spirit of data mesh.

questions.stem: Which role can create a new domain?

options.text: Any user with a Pro license

questions.explanation: Fabric administrators create domains and assign their domain admins. Domain admins and contributors then manage the domain and assign workspaces to it.

questions.stem: A workspace admin is a contributor of the Finance domain and wants their workspace to belong to it. Where do they do this?

options.text: In each item's settings, one by one
In the workspace's settings, by choosing the Finance domain

questions.explanation: Domain contributors can assign workspaces they are admins of to the domain from the workspace's own settings.

questions.stem: Which two are benefits of organizing workspaces into domains? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Workspaces in a domain no longer need capacity
People can find data by business area, for example by filtering the OneLake catalog by domain
Domain admins can manage some settings for their own domain instead of the whole tenant
Every user in a domain becomes an admin of its workspaces
Data in a domain is encrypted with a key only that domain holds

questions.explanation: Domains help people discover data by business area and let some governance be delegated to domain admins. They don't grant workspace roles, add encryption or remove the need for capacity.
